goal: mc is one page and eight verbs now. The code underneath is still the product it was before: a session manager with a registry, a broker, a PTY host, managed providers, cloud runtimes and a capability dispatcher. Measured on 2026-08-29, **71 % of `src/` is not reached by anything the page or its verbs do.**
This project removes that half. Not by grepping for what looks unused — by taking the verb away first and then deleting what the verb was the only reason for. `vault/` stays; see the contract.
contract: **`vault/` stays.** `src/vault/`, `src/cli/vault.js` and `mc vault` are out of scope for deletion this round, whatever reachability says about them — and it does say something: `src/vault/credential-domain/` (3 649 lines, 2 files) is not reached even by `mc vault`, only by the broker world this project removes. Keeping vault means keeping those two files too, deliberately and with a note, not by accident.

**The verb goes first, then the code.** A deletion is only allowed because a verb was removed in an earlier step and the graph shows nothing else reaches the file. No file is deleted because it reads as legacy.
**One cut, one PR.** `mc` and `mc run --rounds 1` work after each. A step that cannot keep both working stops and says so.

**Measured, never assumed.** `reach.mjs` is the evidence; each step reports its before/after numbers in the PR body. decided here — it deletes 22 test files to escape load-flakiness, and ruling `mc-test-1` says the cause is memoro-cli's uncapped `npm test` concurrency and must be re-measured first. The `mc test` split (same ruling) is its own project. The memoro repository is untouched.
**Nothing merges to main without Martin.** No force-push, no rewritten history.

steps.title: The handoff concept
steps.done_when: The workarea handoff concept is gone from the code, the roles and the documentation: no handoff entry in FILING_DIRECTORIES, no ../HANDOFF.md in any prompt, and nothing describing either as current.
instruction: **The handoff concept.** Three sites, zero writers — `plan.js:107`, `canon/roles/plan.md:19`, `work-area.js:55`. Then the 5 `HANDOFF.md` and 3 `handoff/` under `~/mc`. Order matters: the files before the `FILING_DIRECTORIES` entry, or the directories surface on the page as repositories that are not repositories in between.
comments: **The handoff is a reader with no writer**

**The handoff is a reader with no writer.** `grep -rn "HANDOFF.md" src/` returns exactly one line, and it is a *read* instruction in `mc plan`'s first prompt (`src/mc/commands/plan.js:107`), repeated in `canon/roles/plan.md:19`. Nothing in mc has ever written one. It entered with `b4a206a` (#414). Five of ~60 workareas have one, because the prompt told each planning session that the last one might have left one. `src/mc/work-area.js:48` writes the idea down — *"`handoff/` is where a conversation leaves its baton for the next one"* — and `FILING_DIRECTORIES` (`:55`) exists to keep that directory off the page. A filter against a directory nothing creates. mc already has the whole chain this was invented to replace: `decisions/` → `**Beslut:**` → `mc plan` → PLAN.md, which has a section called *What the code taught us* → `mc run` → close-out → `project_log.md`. A handoff is what gets written when the plan is not trusted to carry the work, and it dies with the workarea, which is exactly when someone wants it.
**The inbox is real, and still legacy**

**The inbox is real, and still legacy.** Unlike the handoff it has writers — `work-send.js:176 inboxPath` and `repo-freshen.js` — and one live path in: `repo-gate.js`, `commands/suite.js` and `commands/repo.js` call `tellHolder` (`lease-refusal.js:19`), which drops a line in the suite-lease holder's `inbox/` and knocks on their tmux. That is the PM-era answer to "another session is holding the lease". With `mc run` owning both lanes inside one process, the session to be woken is the one asking.
**Two things wear the same word and must not be swept together**

**Two things wear the same word and must not be swept together.** `src/mc/handoff.js`, `session-runtime-*.js`, `handoff-controller-capability.js` and `src/runtime/broker/handoff-switch-journal.js` are the *provider* handoff — codex↔claude session switching, `mc-session-handoff-v1`. Different feature. It falls in step 4 with the rest of the broker world, on the reachability evidence, not on its name.
**Why the first measurement was wrong**

**Why the first measurement was wrong.** Seeding the graph with the `status` verb pulls `src/cli/status.js`, and from there the entire v1 world: it reported 244 files and 72 703 lines "live". `mc status <name>` is live but reaches the page through a v1 shim. Anything measuring this must seed from `mc/commands/home.js` and the `mc/commands/*` verbs, never from the router's `modules` map — the map is the thing being cut.

steps.title: The verb list
steps.done_when: Not stated in the plan as written — when this step is finished is for the plan review to settle.
instruction: **The verb list.** Decide the surviving set and remove the rest from the `modules` map, `CAPABILITIES`, `src/mc/help-text.js` and `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`. **Nothing is deleted from `src/` in this step** — it is the step that makes step 4 mechanical and each cut reversible by one revert. Re-run `reach.mjs`; its output is the work-list for step 4.
comments: **What survived, and why.** `src/mc-cli.js` keeps twelve verbs — `status`, `work`, `repo`, `merge`, `test`, `worker`, `brief`, `helper`, `plan`, `run`, `roles`, `log` — and `src/bin-mc.js` keeps one, `mc vault`. The rule was the one the plan's first success criterion states: a verb stays if the page or another surviving verb reaches its implementation. `doctor` reaches `dev-servers.js`, `enforcement.js` and `session-maintenance-v1.js`; `migrate` reaches `session-cutover.js` and `session-home-lock.js`; every capability verb reaches `src/cli/`, `src/capabilities/` or `src/adapters/`. All of those are on step 4's list, so keeping their doors would have meant keeping the rooms. `mc log` was the one judgement call in the other direction: it is not in `reach.mjs`'s original seed list but the help names it, `mc-cli.js` writes an `mc.start`/`mc.end` pair on **every** invocation, and `mc log --open` is how a gate round that died is found. It reaches only `src/mc/` files that nothing else on step 4's list touches, so it costs the cut nothing.
**The two tables were 14 and 14, not 29 and 16.** The plan's numbers were measured on 2026-08-29 and PRs #538, #539 and #540 shrank both tables in between. Twenty-eight became thirteen here.

**`src/cli/status.js` is a trap for step 4.** It is the target of the surviving `status` verb, and step 4's instruction says to delete `src/cli/`. It is a 42-line shim now — it prints where the page went and hands a named project to `mc/commands/status-project.js`; the v1 world it used to pull in is gone. So step 4 must either keep it beside `cli/vault.js`, or fold its message into `mc-cli.js`'s own `moved()` and delete it. `reach.mjs` now seeds it by name so it does not appear on the work-list as dead.

**`src/bin.js` is a second one.** It is unreached and 117 lines, so `reach.mjs` lists it — but `package.json`'s `bin` maps both `memoro` and `memoro-cli` to it. Deleting it is deleting two of the three installed commands. That is a decision, not a cleanup, and step 4 should leave it alone or raise it.

**What `reach.mjs` says now.** 274 files / 79 126 lines in `src/`; 90 files / 20 938 lines reached by the page and its verbs; 103 / 25 562 with `bin-mc.js` and `cli/vault.js` added; **171 files / 53 564 lines unreached — 68 % of `src/`**. Before this step: 178 / 54 784, 69 %. The two that moved into the unreached set are exactly `src/mc/commands/doctor.js` and `src/mc/commands/migrate.js`. The seed list was rewritten to the surviving table, and the page's own reach now stops at `bin-mc.js`: `mc-cli.js` falls through to it, so crossing that edge folded the contract's vault cost into the page's number and printed the same figure on both rows.

**How this was verified.** The 25 test files `scripts/affected-tests.js` selects for this diff: 336 tests, 336 passing. `mc` prints the page. `mc run --rounds 1 --no-merge --no-caffeinate` completes a round against a temporary `MC_WORK_ROOT` — isolated on purpose, because the real runner was live and a second one writing `runner.json` would have claimed work. The full 246-file `npm test` was **not** run: main carries a standing red set, and ruling `mc-test-1` says the cause is this repository's uncapped concurrency and must be re-measured before it is trusted.

**One pre-existing red found on the way.** `tests/mc/commands/dormant.test.js` still asserts that `mc pm` and `mc pm-helper` print a dormant line; #540 removed both verbs, so the router answers `unknown command` and the file fails on `main` today. It is not in this diff's affected set. It belongs to step 5 — the tests that only covered deleted code — and it is named here so step 5 does not have to find it twice.

steps.title: Delete what step 3 orphaned
steps.done_when: Not stated in the plan as written — when this step is finished is for the plan review to settle.
instruction: **Delete what step 3 orphaned**, one directory per PR, re-measuring after each: `src/cli/`, `src/runtime/`, `src/adapters/`, `src/capabilities/`, `src/commands/`, then the `src/mc/` half — `session-*`, `registry.js`, `session-home.js`, `owned-resource*`, `managed-*`, `cloud*`, `dev-servers.js`, `cloudflare-guard.js`, `release-trust.js`, `dependencies.js`.
comments: **The cut, measured.** `src/` went from 280 files / 80 889 lines to 151 / 40 617, and `reach.mjs` from 173 files / 53 909 lines unreached (67 %) to none. 130 source files went, with 103 test files, three security probes, the C1 release-contract script and its three assets. The starting numbers differ from step 3's (274 / 79 126) because `origin/main` moved between the two steps; the percentages are the comparable figures.

**One PR, not one per directory.** The instruction asks for a PR per directory and the runner gives a step one PR, so the split is by commit instead: `capabilities`, `adapters`, `runtime`, `cli`, `core`, `mc`, then the tests and the scripts. Only the last commit is a tree that runs. The unreached set imports across its own directories — `cli/cloud-runtime.js` imports the broker, `mc/session-cutover.js` imports the session host — so no single directory can be removed on its own and leave the rest loadable. That is a property of the code, not of the order chosen here.

**What no import graph could see.** Three files are spawned as child processes by a path literal: `lib/update-check-worker.js` from `lib/update-check.js`, `mc/nightly-run.js` from `mc/nightly.js`, `mc/repo-watch-run.js` from `mc/repo-watch.js`. All three were on `reach.mjs`'s unreached list and all three are load-bearing — deleting `nightly-run.js` would have left `mc repo nightly start` spawning a file that is not there, and the parent only ever checks the child's command line afterwards. They were found by grepping every `.js` path literal in the surviving files against the deletion list, which is the check a static graph cannot do for itself. `reach.mjs` seeds all three now and says why.

**`memoro` and `memoro-cli` are the one decision this step left standing.** `package.json` maps two of its three `bin` entries to `src/bin.js`, and `main` to `src/index.js`. Between them they reach 20 files / 3 664 lines that no mc verb touches: `src/commands/` whole, five files under `src/lib/`, `src/mc/session-projector.js` (773 lines), `src/mc/git.js`, `src/mc/open-question.js`, and `runtime/broker/client.js` and `paths.js`. The contract's first rule decides it here — no step of this project removed a `memoro` verb, so nothing `memoro` reaches may be deleted under it. Whether those two commands should still ship is a product decision rather than a cleanup; the README documents them under *low-level surface*. They are now the largest single thing between mc and a `src/` that is only mc, and `reach.mjs` counts them on their own row.

**Keeping vault cost about two and a half times what the contract estimated.** Beyond `credential-domain/`'s two files (3 649 lines), 13 more stay because those two import them at module top level: six `adapters/managed-runtime/` files, `capabilities/github/github-contract.js`, `runtime/broker/c1-artifacts.js`, `c1-process-group.js` and `c1-source-closure.js`, and `mc/managed-generation-journal.js`, `managed-provider-archive.js` and `runtime-secrets.js` — roughly 5 400 lines of exactly the broker world the goal removes. Deleting them would have left two files the contract keeps unable to load at all. Nothing reaches any of it: it is a preserved carcass, which is what the contract asked for, and it is bigger than the contract said.

**The C1 custody chain is split in half by the contract, and was already failing closed before this step.** `vault/engine/c1-claude-lease.js` spawns `runtime/broker/c1-child.js` by path and pins its SHA-256 in its own source, so the child is kept — the same kind of edge as `nightly.js` → `nightly-run.js`. What the child dynamically imports one layer further in is not kept: the managed-claude C1 harness pulls the C1 runtime, which pulls `claude-managed-policy.js`. That costs nothing, because `c1-source-closure.js`'s pinned digests for `package.json` and `src/mc/paths.js` already did not match `main` — `verifyInstalledC1SourceClosure()` was returning failure before this step touched anything, which is why `tests/runtime/broker/c1-source-closure.test.js` is red on main today. `scripts/security/check-c1-source-closure.mjs` walked from three files this step deleted, so it went with them and `npm run security:c1-source-closure` with it. `credential-boundary-probe.mjs` stays: its subject is `codex-managed.js`, which vault keeps.

**Two vault tests went with the world they reach into.** `tests/vault/credential-domain/local-claude.test.js` and `local-codex.test.js` import `src/mc/managed-provider-registry.js`, and keeping that alive pulls the managed registration halves and the artifact writers back with it — measured, not guessed. `tests/adapters/managed-runtime/codex-managed.test.js` builds its fixture out of `src/adapters/artifacts/`. The contract keeps vault's source and it does: both `credential-domain` files still load, and `tests/vault/engine/c1-claude-lease.test.js` still passes in full, which is why the C1 child was kept.

**The tests went in this step rather than step 5, and step 5 still has work.** 103 test files could no longer be loaded at all — an import of a deleted module throws before a single case runs, so leaving them would have made `npm test` unloadable rather than red, and no PR measuring this diff could have landed. What is left for step 5 is what still loads: six files that fail — `cli/lifecycle/auth-status`, `cli/lifecycle/deps`, `mc/commands/dormant` (step 3 named it), `mc/fresh-session`, `runtime/broker/c1-source-closure`, `runtime/certified-execution/credential-boundary` — all six of them red on `main` before this step; plus every test that still passes while covering behaviour nothing runs, plus `#410`'s rebase. Two survivors lost their only direct coverage: `src/mc/paths.js`, which the rest of the suite exercises transitively, and `runtime/broker/client.js`, which is kept only for `src/bin.js`.

**`scripts/mc-release-smoke.js` is dead and was left alone.** It drives `mc auth status`, `mc tool-switch`, `mc new`, `mc resume` and `mc fanout`, none of which exist; `npm run smoke:mc` still points at it. Nothing this step deleted broke it — it was already a release smoke of a product that is gone, so it is named here rather than removed under a step whose rule is that the verb goes first.

**Verifying `mc run` starts real work, and the next session should know it before trying.** `mc run --rounds 1 --no-merge --no-caffeinate` with `MC_WORK_ROOT` and `MC_HOME` pointed at temporary directories still reads the plans on `origin/main` and still creates worktrees in the real repositories from them: the round ran the helper digest, wrote intake, computed lanes (memoro 34, memoro-cli 3), created two workareas and dispatched two live `claude` step sessions before it was killed. Two branches survive that, both sitting exactly on their repository's `origin/main` with no commits: `mc-cut-4` in memoro-cli, whose worktree was removed, and `email-verification-round-3` in memoro, whose worktree at `/private/tmp/mc-work-pfF9/email-verification-round/memoro` is still registered — removing either branch, and that worktree, needed permissions this session does not have. There is no dry run: repository roots come from `homedir()`, not from `MC_WORK_ROOT`, so nothing short of a different `$HOME` isolates a round from the real work.

steps.title: `docs/plans/`
steps.done_when: Not stated in the plan as written — when this step is finished is for the plan review to settle.
instruction: **`docs/plans/`** — 34 files describing the dismantled world. Read before deleting: some are the only record of why something was built.
comments: **All 34 were read in full before anything was deleted, and the rule was the criterion's own words.** A file stays only if its subject is machinery that still exists. Two do: `mc-custody.md`, whose S1–S3 are `src/vault/engine/custody-crypto.js`, `key-cache.js` and `tool-auth.js` as shipped and which four source files and four test files already cite by name; and `vault-import.md`, whose `scan`/`import`/`bindings` verbs are still in `src/cli/vault.js`'s `VERBS` map. Thirty-two go — 12 603 of 13 048 lines. Both survivors got a status header saying what is live and what was withdrawn, because neither is wholly true any more: `vault-import.md` plans a materialise-at-launch lifecycle that `mc vault bind` and `mc vault get` now refuse outright, and `mc-custody.md` plans an isolated credential domain and typed adapters that were never built.

**The three documents `docs/coding-agent-protocol.md` called normative were all deleted, and one of them had to survive as prose.** `credential-blind-capabilities.md`'s rule — no vault secret in plaintext to an LLM-controlled process — is live and enforced by the two refusing verbs, so the protocol bullet now states it inline and says it is the normative copy. `connected-capabilities.md` and `github-app-capability.md` (1 507 lines) described a connection registry, broker grants and a GitHub App capability that step 4 deleted whole; their bullets went with them. Same for the `mc-v2-workload-allowlist.md` bullet: it governed cloud workload routes in a runtime that no longer exists here.

**What the protocol still gets wrong, which is not this step's to fix.** `docs/coding-agent-protocol.md` § *GitHub interaction in coding sessions* still describes `mc github` as canonical, a session-scoped `gh` shim, `github-op-v1` broker operations and `MC_HOST_CAPABILITIES` — none of which exist after step 4. `docs/onboarding.md` is worse: the whole file walks `mc setup`, `mc auth status`, `mc install-shell`, `mc new` and `mc end`. Both are outside `docs/plans/`, so this step only re-anchored their dangling links and left the substance alone. The close-out step is where that belongs, or its own project.

**Two live source files cited a deleted plan as their design source, and one thing lost its only record.** `src/lib/device-flow.js` pointed at `worktree-lifecycle.md` §14c/§14f and `src/cli/vault.js` at §12k.1; both comments now say the plan was removed and carry the one fact worth keeping (per-device tokens are `api-tokens` with scope `device`, not a table of their own). §14's device-flow design is now documented nowhere but that file. `src/lib/annotate.js` and its test pointed at `docs/plans/coding-profile.md`, which this repository has never carried — that link was already dangling on main.

**`npm run security:credential-boundary` outlives its plan.** `scripts/security/credential-boundary-probe.mjs` survives (step 4 kept it because its subject `src/adapters/managed-runtime/codex-managed.js` is one of the files vault drags in), but `mc-v2-local-codex-containment.md`, which is the record of what that containment was and its two-generation validation, is deleted: the launch owner it describes — `--managed-portable`, broker protocol v3, per-session credential domains, the exclusive lease — is gone from `src/`. The probe now has no document behind it. I did not run it.

**How this was verified.** `docs/plans/` holds two files, both about the vault. Every `docs/plans/...` reference in the repository was re-checked: no markdown link points at a missing file, and the five remaining bare mentions are either prose that names a file as removed, or the memoro repository's own `msr-*`/`sql-readiness` plans in a test fixture and in `utredning-2026-08-24.md`. `scripts/affected-tests.js` selects **61 files** for this diff — far more than the diff's size suggests, because the selector is documentation-aware and most `tests/mc/` files declare a read of `docs/coding-agent-protocol.md` and `docs/onboarding.md`, both of which this step edits, while the vault suites `pin` `docs/plans/mc-custody.md` by name. 851 tests, 842 passing, 0 failing, 9 skipped. `mc` prints the page. The full `npm test` was not run — main carries a standing red set and ruling `mc-test-1` says its cause must be re-measured first — and `mc run --rounds 1` was not run: this diff is documentation only, it touches no file `mc run` loads, and step 4's comment records that a round cannot be isolated from the real repositories.

steps.title: Close-out
steps.done_when: Not stated in the plan as written — when this step is finished is for the plan review to settle.
instruction: **Close-out** — `docs/technical/mc-cut.md`, the `project_log.md` row, and `reach.mjs` either kept as the guard it became or removed with a note.
comments: **`reach.mjs` is kept, and it had to move to be kept.** It lived in this plan's own directory, and `mc run` deletes that directory in the round it reads `done` — so leaving it there would have been the *removed* option taken by accident rather than the *kept* one chosen. It is `scripts/reach.mjs` now, with `npm run reach` and `npm run reach -- --list` in `package.json`. Two changes beyond the move: the root argument now skips a leading flag, because `npm run reach -- --list` passes `--list` as `argv[2]` and the old code would have resolved it as the repository root; and the header no longer cites step numbers of a plan that is about to stop existing. It is deliberately not in `npm test` — a file added mid-change is legitimately unreached until that change lands, and a test going red for it would gate ordinary work rather than drift.

**The four sets in the note are a partition, not four overlapping readings.** `reach.mjs` prints cumulative rows, which is right for watching a cut but reads badly as an inventory, so the note gives the disjoint split: the page and its twelve verbs 101 files / 23 354 lines, `mc vault`'s own door 13 / 4 628, vault's carcass 19 / 9 451, `memoro` + `memoro-cli` 20 / 3 665 — 153 / 41 098 exactly. Computed with the same graph and the same seeds, not by subtracting the printed rows by hand.

**Vault's carcass is not a preserved capability, and the note says so.** Step 4 kept 13 files beyond `credential-domain/` because those two import them at module top level. Reading them for this note turned up that the kept code cannot run either way: `local-codex.js`'s `MANAGED_GITHUB_RUNTIME_PATHS` names `src/capabilities/github/github-session.js`, `github-shim.js` and `github-write-client.js`, and its launch path `realpathSync`s `src/adapters/artifacts/codex.js` — four files step 4 deleted, in a list that is digested rather than imported, so no import graph and no load-time error could have shown it. That is the same shape as `c1-source-closure.js`'s pinned digests already not matching `main`. Read, not run: nothing here was executed.

**What this step fixed beyond the three things it was asked for, and why.** Step 6's comments handed `docs/coding-agent-protocol.md` and `docs/onboarding.md` to "the close-out step … or its own project". I took the protocol and left the other two. The protocol is the file every session in this repository is told to read first, and it was instructing them to publish through `mc github`, a `gh` shim and a Memoro GitHub App operation that this project deleted — a defect mc-cut created in the one normative document.
